subject: Incident notification & forensic deliverables — proposed timeline and scope
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Incident notification & forensic deliverables — proposed timeline and scope

Marta / Greenline team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation we wanted to capture a pragmatic proposal to close the gap between your current DPA expectations and what Redwood can operationally deliver without broadening legal/compliance risk. High-level ask: confirm whether Greenline can accept the compromise below or if legal needs a different path.

Proposed operational notification flow (Redwood suggestion):
- Preliminary acknowledgement: Redwood will acknowledge receipt of a verified incident notification within 24 hours of detection/notification.
- Substantive update: Redwood will provide an initial substantive update (scope, affected data classes, preliminary mitigation) within 72 hours.
- Forensic package: deliver a forensic summary and preserved artifacts within 5 business days; a more detailed final report within 10 business days for EU customers.

Scope and limitations we propose:
- Deliverables: preserved event timelines, schema-mapped logs (redacted/anonymized), affected tenant/object identifiers in hashed form, ingestion/transit slices, and export-ready snapshot of telemetry.
- Red lines: Redwood cannot export customer plaintext keys or raw KMS-protected secrets. Raw, unredacted user content or private keys will be produced only in response to a lawful process (court order/subpoena) or under a separate escrow arrangement.
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide an up-to-date subprocessor list and commit to reasonable cooperation with forensics requests that require subprocessor engagement. Cross-border exports will be governed by SCCs or other lawful transfer mechanisms.

Attachments: Ive attached a draft redline of the incident clause and an incident contact matrix so we can align on operational handoffs.

If this direction is acceptable, Kim / Ben / I will produce a redline you can sign off or escalate to your counsel. Please advise if Greenline needs a faster acknowledgement cadence or additional on-site interaction language (e.g., remote-live queries vs. full dataset export).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Subject: Re: Incident notification & forensic deliverables — proposed timeline and scope

Jordan,

Appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from Greenline Legal / InfoSec:
- Timing: Greenline requires initial disclosure to the customer within 48 hours of detection of a confirmed incident that materially impacts our data, with a substantive update within 72 hours and a final investigatory report within 10 calendar days (we can be flexible on business days vs. calendar days if you document the assumption).
- Evidence scope: we need access to raw logs covering the affected time window, exported in a format that preserves timestamps and correlation IDs. We understand redaction constraints but request practical paths to review unredacted logs (e.g., Redacted export + secure remote session with your forensics team).
- Key material: due to patient-safety concerns at Greenline, we need to reserve the right to request KMS-wrapped metadata and key identifiers to validate scope; we do not expect receipt of customers' encryption keys but need metadata about key usage.
- Subprocessors: we expect confirmation of which subprocessors were in-scope and a point of contact to engage them rapidly.

Were willing to accept a compromise where Redwood provides a secure, supervised remote query session on unredacted logs and a machine-readable export of anonymized data. Can you confirm whether that is technically feasible and how long it would take? If not feasible, well need contract language committing to produce raw logs on lawful compulsion.

Marta
Head of Security & Privacy, Greenline Health
marta.lopez@greenlinehealth.com

Team,

Ive drafted a compromise clause and included operational guardrails in the attached redline. Key points below for alignment before we respond to Greenline:

1) Notification windows
- Customer notification by Redwood: Redwood will acknowledge receipt of a reported incident within 24 hours of confirmation of a security event and provide a substantive update within 72 hours; final investigatory findings within 10 business days for EU accounts unless extended by mutual written agreement.

2) Forensic deliverables & access
- Redwood to provide: (a) schema-normalized logs, (b) hashed identifiers (salted per-customer), (c) preserved snapshots of relevant system state, (d) aggregated telemetry and correlation maps.
- Remote supervised queries: Redwood will offer a secure, read-only remote query session with its forensics engineers for Greenline to run queries against preserved datasets under NDA. This avoids broad plaintext exports but enables validation.
- Raw export exception: Redwood will comply with lawful process. Where Greenline requires raw exports beyond the scope above, Redwood will consider a separate forensic access addendum or escrow arrangement; any such export will be subject to execution of supplemental agreements and indemnities.

3) Subprocessor coordination & transfers
- Redwood will identify subprocessors engaged during the relevant time window and, where needed, coordinate approvals/engagements. Cross-border transfers will rely on SCCs and documented lawful bases.

4) Escalation/SLAs
- For incidents meeting customer-critical criteria (e.g., affecting PHI), Redwood will trigger an executive escalation with a named SLA owner and propose acceleration of deliverable timelines.

Ben: can you confirm the technical feasibility and an estimated lead time to make a supervised query environment available (hours/days)? Vanessa: if Greenline pushes for 48h, will sales be comfortable with the modified 24h ack + 72h update position?

Im attaching the redline and the incident contact matrix for a single-stop operational handoff.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Incident notification & forensic deliverables — proposed timeline and scope

Kim / team,

Technical reality and what we can commit to:
- Supervised remote query: feasible. We can stand up a read-only session against preserved snapshots within 24-48 hours of preservation, depending on load and on-call availability. Session will be time-boxed and monitored.
- Exports: we can produce machine-readable exports of logs with timestamps and correlation IDs; exporting unredacted user content at scale is operationally risky and will need the separate addendum.
- KMS metadata: we can provide key identifiers, usage metadata, and whether an affected object was encrypted under customer-managed keys. We cannot export secret key material.
- Effort: initial preserved snapshot & sanitized schema-normalized export — estimate 2-3 business days to assemble for a medium-sized tenant; supervised query environment setup — 24-48 hours after preservation.

Operational ask: we need Greenline to accept a supervised-query-first route in the contract and acknowledge that raw key material is out of scope except under lawful compulsion. Also recommend a short escalation clause allowing an SLA exception for PHI-impacting incidents so we can mobilize additional engineers.

Ben Carter
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Incident notification & forensic deliverables — proposed timeline and scope

Marta (and Greenline Legal),

Thanks for the prompt feedback and for being willing to discuss constructive tradeoffs. Based on internal review Kim / Ben and I propose the following consolidated contractual language and operational commitment:

- Acknowledgement: Redwood will acknowledge receipt of a confirmed incident affecting Greenlines data within 24 hours.
- Substantive update: Redwood will provide an initial substantive update within 72 hours, describing scope, affected data classes, and mitigation steps.
- Forensic access: Redwood will: (1) preserve relevant snapshots and schema-normalized logs, (2) provide a supervised remote query session for Greenlines authorized forensics/legal team to run read-only queries against preserved datasets within 48 hours of preservation, and (3) deliver a machine-readable anonymized export (hashed IDs, timestamps, correlation IDs) within 5 business days.
- Raw key/export limitation: Redwood will not export plaintext customer encryption keys or KMS-protected secrets. Metadata about key usage and key identifiers will be provided. Any request for raw, unredacted content or keys will require a separate, executed forensic access addendum or lawful compulsion.
- Subprocessors & transfers: Redwood will provide a subprocessor list and coordinate engagement; cross-border transfers will be managed under SCCs or equivalent lawful transfer mechanisms.
- Escalation: For incidents impacting PHI or patient-safety, Redwood commits to immediate executive escalation and will target accelerated timelines; the parties will agree an SLA owner at onboarding.

If Greenline can accept the supervised-query-first approach and the limitation around plaintext keys (with the option for addendum/subpoena), we will return a redline incorporating the above and a DocuSign-ready addendum for the supervised-query operational process.

Can you please confirm (a) whether the 24h ack + 72h substantive + 5 business day evidence timeline is acceptable, and (b) whether Greenline wants the separate forensic-access addendum template included in the redline package?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
